requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
The source and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.references.coverage.report`.

### Obligations and coverage

- **`habeas status` must warn about every item without recent coverage.** `src/commands.rs#fn[inspected_coverage_warnings]` applies the history-based coverage decision through `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`. `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_section]` renders all resulting warnings; its caller, `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]`, includes that section in status. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts both an uncovered item's warning and the absence of a recently covered item's warning. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` verifies immediate warnings for a never-read helper and the transition from covered to warned as the record ages out. This checks application of `requirements.references.coverage.history`, without reassessing that requirement's internal obligations.
- **`habeas author` must issue those warnings after finishing.** `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` prints every warning. Its caller, `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, invokes it after completed batch and single-subject authoring, including the current-record skip path. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` asserts the actual warning after an author command; `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` verifies warnings even when a named current record requires no assessment. The other supplied authoring tests exercise the completed-batch and single-record stdout routes and assert the incomplete-history notice.
- **Each warning must name its file, line, kind, and name.** `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` supplies these values to `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[uncovered_error]`, whose formatted diagnostic preserves all four. The exact warning substring asserted by each of the status and author integration tests above includes all four fields.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` must be excluded.** `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` filters `in_tests` items. `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` computes that flag using `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_module]` and `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_file]`. The reauthoring test's exact warning lists exclude the inline-module helper. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]` verifies out-of-line modules; `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` checks module-file versus crate-root distinctions.
- **A warning must not fail validation.** `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` accumulates uncovered ordinary items separately from validation errors, and `src/commands.rs#fn[inspected_coverage_warnings]` converts them into the separate warning result. The reauthoring test explicitly checks that the warned-about `parse` does not enter validation errors. The author integration test also asserts successful completion despite warnings.
- **Repository validation must not read Git history.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_repository]` returns the report from repository inspection. `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` computes current uncovered items without invoking the historical coverage loader; history is loaded separately by `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` removes committed objects and asserts unchanged validation errors, while confirming that the separate coverage-warning calculation detects incomplete history.

The warning rendering, stderr routing, and incomplete-history notice are within the required reporting behavior and its cited history context. No unacknowledged gap was found.

{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
